lockedSourceMove.claimSummary: Individual moral reasoning is systematically motivated, but well-designed institutions can make reason more reliable through adversarial correction.
lockedSourceMove.reasonSummary: Individuals seek support for desired propositions and stop when they find it, whereas science institutionalizes disconfirmation by letting other motivated reasoners push back.

inferenceSummary.premise: People reason selectively as individuals, while organized criticism exposes unsupported claims.
inferenceSummary.inference: Reliability can emerge from a system even when its individual participants are biased.
inferenceSummary.conclusion: Skepticism about solitary moral reasoning need not entail skepticism about reason itself.
